The park is home to many predatory animals, including [Canada lynx](/wiki/Canada_lynx "Canada lynx"), foxes, [bobcat](/wiki/Bobcat "Bobcat"), [cougar](/wiki/North_American_cougar "North American cougar"), [black bear](/wiki/Cinnamon_bear "Cinnamon bear"), and [coyotes](/wiki/Coyote "Coyote"). Wolves and grizzly bears were extirpated in the early 1900s. Most of these predators kill smaller animals, but mountain lions and coyotes kill deer and occasionally elk. Bears also eat larger prey. Moose have no predators in the park. Black bears are relatively uncommon in the park, numbering only 24–35 animals. They also have fewer cubs and the bears seem skinnier than they do in most areas.[[72]](#cite_note-NPS_bears-73) Canadian lynx are quite rare within the park, and they have probably spread north from the San Juan Mountains, where they were reintroduced in 1999. Cougars feed mainly on mule deer in the park, and live 10–13 years. Cougar territories can be as large as 500 square miles (1,300 km2).[[73]](#cite_note-NPS_mountain_lion-74) Coyotes hunt both alone and in pairs, but occasionally hunt in [packs](/wiki/Pack_(canine) "Pack (canine)"). They mainly feed on rodents but occasionally bring down larger animals, including deer, and especially fawns and elk calves. Scat studies in Moraine Park showed that their primary foods were deer and rodents. They form strong family bonds and are very vocal.[[74]](#cite_note-NPS_coyote-75)

He is buried in tomb number 57, surrounded by tombs of his four wives.

Carlos Alcaraz and [Alexander Zverev](/wiki/Alexander_Zverev "Alexander Zverev") have faced off thirteen times, with Alcaraz leading 7–6.[[247]](#cite_note-248)

They met twice in 2021, with Zverev dismantling a 17–18 year old Alcaraz in both matches. Their first notable match was the final of the [Madrid Open](/wiki/2022_Mutua_Madrid_Open_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_singles "2022 Mutua Madrid Open – Men's singles") in 2022, where Alcaraz swept past defending champion Zverev in one hour and four minutes.[[248]](#cite_note-249) A few weeks later they had their first major meeting in the [French Open](/wiki/2022_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_singles "2022 French Open – Men's singles") quarterfinals, where Zverev defeated Alcaraz in four sets.[[249]](#cite_note-250) They had further high profile encounters in the quarterfinals of the [2023 US Open](/wiki/2023_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_singles "2023 US Open – Men's singles"), won by Alcaraz, and the quarterfinals of the [2024 Australian Open](/wiki/2024_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_singles "2024 Australian Open – Men's singles"), won by Zverev.

In 2024 they met for the [French Open](/wiki/2024_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_singles "2024 French Open – Men's singles") final, where Zverev was hunting for his first major title. Zverev took a two-sets-to-one lead, but Alcaraz outlasted him to win in five sets and claim his first French Open title.[[250]](#cite_note-251)

In the semifinals of the [2026 Australian Open](/wiki/2026_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_singles "2026 Australian Open – Men's singles"), Alcaraz took a two-set lead before struggling due to cramps. Zverev won the next two sets in a pair of tiebreaks, but Alcaraz recovered in time to win the fifth set, proceeding to his maiden Australian Open final. At 5 hours and 27 minutes, this was the longest Australian Open semifinal in history.[[251]](#cite_note-252)

The first climb on Makalu was made by an American team led by Riley Keegan in the spring of 1954. The expedition was composed of [Sierra Club](/wiki/Sierra_Club "Sierra Club") members including Bill Long and [Allen Steck](/wiki/Allen_Steck "Allen Steck"), and was called the California Himalayan Expedition to Makalu.[[5]](#cite_note-Sierra2005-6)
They attempted the southeast ridge but were forced to turn back at 7,100 metres (23,300 ft) by a constant barrage of storms. A New Zealand team including [Sir Edmund Hillary](/wiki/Edmund_Hillary "Edmund Hillary") was also active in the spring, but did not get very high due to injury and illness. In the fall of 1954, a French reconnaissance expedition made the first ascents of the subsidiary summits Kangchungtse (October 22: Jean Franco, [Lionel Terray](/wiki/Lionel_Terray "Lionel Terray"), [sirdar](/wiki/Sardar#Modern_usage "Sardar") Gyalzen Norbu Sherpa and Pa Norbu) and Chomo Lonzo (likely on October 30: [Jean Couzy](/wiki/Jean_Couzy "Jean Couzy") and Terray).[[6]](#cite_note-baume-7)

Segrè enlisted his colleague Perrier to attempt to prove, through comparative chemistry, that the molybdenum activity was indeed from an element with the atomic number 43, which they did. [University of Palermo](/wiki/University_of_Palermo "University of Palermo") officials wanted them to name their discovery *panormium*, after the Latin name for [Palermo](/wiki/Palermo "Palermo"), **Panormus**. Segrè returned to Berkeley and met [Glenn T. Seaborg](/wiki/Glenn_T._Seaborg "Glenn T. Seaborg"). General LeMay conversed with President Kennedy at the [Oval Office](/wiki/Oval_Office "Oval Office"), [White House](/wiki/White_House "White House") in October 1962.

LeMay was bitterly critical of the Kennedy administration. He described the so-called "[Whiz Kids](/wiki/Whiz_Kids_(Department_of_Defense) "Whiz Kids (Department of Defense)")" in the U.S. Department of Defense as "the most egotistical people that I have ever seen in my whole life. They had no faith in the military at all. They felt that the [Harvard Business School](/wiki/Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School") method of solving problems would solve any problem in the world."[[50]](#cite_note-51)

During the [Cuban Missile Crisis](/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis "Cuban Missile Crisis") in 1962, LeMay clashed again with U.S. President [John F. Kennedy](/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") and Secretary of Defense [Robert McNamara](/wiki/Robert_McNamara_as_Secretary_of_Defense "Robert McNamara as Secretary of Defense"), arguing that he should be allowed to bomb nuclear missile sites in [Cuba](/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"). He opposed the naval [blockade](/wiki/Blockade "Blockade") and, after the end of the crisis, suggested that Cuba be invaded anyway, even after the Soviets agreed to withdraw their missiles. Kennedy refused LeMay's requests, and the naval blockade was successful.[[51]](#cite_note-Rhodes575-52)

LeMay told Kennedy that his refusal to invade Cuba was "almost as bad as the [appeasement at Munich](/wiki/Lesson_of_Munich "Lesson of Munich")"[[52]](#cite_note-53) and the "greatest defeat in our history."[[53]](#cite_note-54) Twenty-five years later, LeMay still believed that "We could have gotten not only the missiles out of Cuba, we could have gotten the Communists out of Cuba at that time."[[54]](#cite_note-jstor2538995-55)

De'Aaron Fox :: Professional career :: Sacramento Kings (2017–2025) :: Early years (2017–2019) :: chunk_0003
On June 22, 2017, Fox was selected with the fifth overall pick in the [2017 NBA draft](/wiki/2017_NBA_draft "2017 NBA draft") by the [Sacramento Kings](/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings"). The team also selected former teammate [Justin Jackson](/wiki/Justin_Jackson_(basketball,_born_1995) "Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1995)") in the same round.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

On July 8, 2017, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Kings.[[21]](#cite_note-21) During four games of the [2017 NBA Summer League](/wiki/2017_NBA_Summer_League "2017 NBA Summer League"), Fox averaged 11.8 points, 3 assists and 2.3 steals while playing 21.3 minutes per game. Fox made his NBA debut for the Kings in their season opener on October 18, 2017, against the [Houston Rockets](/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets"), where he scored 14 points, 4 rebounds, and 5 assist in 24-plus minutes in a 105–100 loss.[[22]](#cite_note-22) On October 23, 2017, Fox recorded a career-high 19 points, 4 assist, 5 rebounds, and 3 steals in a 117–115 loss against the [Phoenix Suns](/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns"). On December 8, 2017, he scored 14 points, 4 assist and 2 steals in a 116–109 win against the [New Orleans Pelicans](/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans"). On January 6, 2018, Fox recorded 18 points and 7 assist in a 106–98 victory over the [Denver Nuggets](/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets"). On January 25, 2018, Fox scored 14 points, 4 assist and a putback [slam dunk](/wiki/Slam_dunk "Slam dunk") with 3.3 seconds left giving the [Sacramento Kings](/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings") the lead in an 89–88 win over the [Miami Heat](/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat"). On January 28, 2018, Fox scored a season-high 26 points, going 6–6 from three-point range in a 15-point loss to the [San Antonio Spurs](/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs").[[23]](#cite_note-23) On February 14, Fox was named [Lonzo Ball](/wiki/Lonzo_Ball "Lonzo Ball")'s replacement for the [Rising Stars Challenge](/wiki/Rising_Stars_Challenge "Rising Stars Challenge").
